meta.title: Practical tips for working with AI tools in an Irish hospital
meta.description: Plain advice for hospital administrators and nursing staff: unapproved tools, checking AI drafts, vendor answers, incident cards and telling patients about AI.
meta.lead: These are the author’s practical suggestions, not legal requirements. Where a document applies, the page says so and names it.

sections.heading: Do not paste patient information into tools you have not approved
sections.body: Names, PPS numbers, dates of birth, phone numbers and the contents of records should stay out of consumer chatbots. The Data Protection Commission’s AI guidance warns that personal data typed into AI tools can raise security and data protection risks, and that some models can reproduce training data. Say clearly which tools are approved.

sections.heading: Keep a list of AI tools and a name beside each
sections.body: HIQA’s January 2026 draft suggests a list of authorised AI tools shared with staff and an individual assigned to keep an inventory. A shared spreadsheet is a fine start.

sections.heading: Check AI drafts the way you would check a trainee’s first draft
sections.body: AI can state wrong things confidently. The Data Protection Commission notes outputs relied on without human review create automated decision-making risks. Check facts, numbers and names against the source before anything enters a record.

sections.heading: Ask vendors three questions in writing
sections.body: Is it a medical device and why or why not? Where does our data go and is it re-used? How will you tell us about a fault or a software update? Keep the answers with the contract.

sections.heading: Put the clocks on one card
sections.body: A serious device incident goes to HPRA (HPRA sets no hospital deadline, so decide your own). A personal data breach has a 72-hour clock for the controller under GDPR Article 33. A serious incident with a high-risk AI system goes to the provider first, then to the authorities (AI Act Article 26(5)). Put who does what on one page.

sections.heading: Tell patients when AI is part of their care
sections.body: HIQA’s draft and the AI for Care strategy both stress transparency about when, where and why AI is used. Decide in advance who explains it and what the short answer is.
